title: A pumi plugin's package.json
description: The `pumi` key of a plugin's package.json: what the plugin is and what it contributes, read without running it. The rest of package.json is npm's.

displayName.description: Its name as people read it (`Chat UI`), which Settings and the store show instead of `pumi.name` (`chat-ui`). Beside `pumi`, so a pumi that does not know it still loads the plugin.

name.description: The plugin's name; its id is `owner/name`, and its prefix `owner.name.`.

owner.description: The owner of a linked local plugin (`local` without one). A published plugin's owner is its GitHub owner, lowercased with `-` as `_`.

api.description: The API level the plugin is written for. Without it the plugin is not run.

minPumi.description: The oldest pumi release it runs on.

isolate.description: Run it in a process of its own on the same Bun, instead of a worker.

uses.description: What it says it touches, shown before it is installed. Nothing is enforced.

themes.description: Its UI themes: directories in the plugin, each with a `theme.ts` (its default export a theme, `defineTheme`), its `*.css` and a `preview.png` or `.svg`. A theme's id is its directory's name, what `ui_theme` is set to.

icon.description: Its icon in the store: a square PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF in the plugin (256×256 is plenty).

images.description: What its store listing shows: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG files in the plugin. The first is its card's picture, cropped to 16:10.

activation.description: When its worker starts. Without any, it starts on first use of one of its contributions.

Contributes.description: What the plugin adds, read from the manifest without running it.

options.description: Its options, by key: `side_by_side` is `owner.name.side_by_side`. Options exist only here.

keys.description: Default keys, each running one of its commands.

slots.description: What it adds to the window's slots, by slot: actions (each runs one of its commands) and a component (an export of src/ui.tsx, loaded when the slot is on screen). `palette.actions` holds actions only.

component.description: The export of src/ui.tsx that draws it.

command.description: One of its `commands`, run with what the slot is of (`{tab}`, `{view}`).

blocks.description: The blocks it defines: `owner.name.<id>`, each drawn by the src/ui.tsx export named for its id (`board` → `Board`).

icon.description: What its tabs show for it until one sets its own `@icon`: one of the app's icons by name, a `data:image/…` URI, or `plugin:<path>`, an SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF file in the plugin. An SVG is tinted by the theme.

version.description: The version of its tabs' saved `data`; a state of another version is refused. 1 by default.

strategy.description: How its tabs come back: as they were, by running something again, or pointing at something that must still exist. `exact` by default.

methods.description: Its tabs' own methods: `tab.call(tab, method, args)` fires `tab.called` for the renderer and answers `null`.

engine.description: What the core runs its tabs on. `terminal`: a PTY and its program, opened with `{command, cwd, env, keep}`, relaunched when it comes back, and carried across a restart. Its renderer draws `<terminal tab>`; with none, the window does. Without an engine, the plugin draws and answers its tabs.

renderers.description: The blocks it draws but did not define (the core's `file`, another plugin's `owner.name.id`), each with the src/ui.tsx export that draws them. A renderer of `file` may say which files it draws: `{"export": "Editor", "match": ["*.md"]}`; the one whose glob fits a file best draws it, unless the tab's `@tab_renderer` names another.

match.description: Globs: one without a `/` is matched against the file's name, one with a `/` against its path (from any folder, unless it starts with `/`). `*` is any run of characters but `/`, `**` any at all, `?` one; case is ignored. The most literal characters of a matching glob is how well it fits.

traits.description: Its traits, `owner.name.<id>`: a tab has one while its option `@owner.name.<id>` is set.

settings.description: What it draws in Settings: pages of its own (after the built-in ones in the nav) and sections on a page (a built-in one, after its own rows, or one of its pages), each an export of src/ui.tsx drawn with the settings kit (`Page`, `Section`, `Row`, `OptionRow`, … from "pumi"). Without `settings`, its options are a page Settings makes of them. A page's and a section's id is prefixed as its options are (`tailscale` is `owner.name.tailscale`): what `openSettings` links to and `registry.list("settings")` lists.

component.description: The export of src/ui.tsx that draws it, loaded when the page is shown.

keywords.description: Words Settings' search finds it by, beside its title.

page.description: A built-in page (`general`, `appearance`, `keys`, `plugins`) or the id of one of its own `pages`.

component.description: The export of src/ui.tsx that draws it, loaded when its page is shown.

keywords.description: Words Settings' search finds it by, beside its title.

OptionSpec.description: An option's declaration: `option.declare`'s fields, with `secret` for a value kept in the OS keychain.

default.description: Its value until one is set; not kept for a `secret`.

scope.description: The narrowest object it is set on; `global` by default.

label.description: Its title in Settings; made of its key by default.

group.description: Its heading in Settings; the plugin's name by default.

choices.description: The values it accepts, when only some are allowed.

labels.description: What Settings calls each of `choices`, in their order.

placeholder.description: What an empty text field shows.

control.description: How Settings edits it when its type does not say.

types.description: The tab types it belongs to (one of its own components by its id); every tab's when empty.
